question.problem: The radius of the base of a cone is decreasing at a rate of $4\,\text{m}/\text{h}.$ The height of the cone is always half its radius. At what rate is the cone's volume decreasing when the radius of its base is $12\,\text{m}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's call $h$ the height of the cone and $r$ the radius of its base. Both of these quantities, as well as the volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-4\,\text{m}/\text{h},
$$

and we need to find $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$ when $r=12\,\text{m}.$

We need to find a relation between $v$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $r.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $h$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $h$ in terms of $r.$

We're told that the height of the cone is half its radius. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}h & =\frac{r}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}\cdot (\frac{r}{2})=\frac{1}{6}\pi {r}^{3}.
$$

Now that we have an equation relating just $v$ and $r,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{6}\pi {r}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi (12)^{2}(-4) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =-288\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the cone's volume is decreasing at a rate of $288\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}/\text{h}.$
